learning_outcomes.text: Understanding of fundamental principles and assumptions of fracture mechanics
Learning the analytical and computational methods needed to solve the idealized problem
Gaining the ability of analyzing the stress around the crack
Learning the fracture toughness test methods

syllabus_topics: Introduction to fracture mechanics, theoretical cohesive strength
The stress concentration factor, external variables affecting fracture
Macroscopic fracture mechanisms and surface examination
Crack tip plastic zone size estimation, design philosophy
Griffith crack theory, energy approach method
Fracture mode transition: Plane stress vs. plane strain
J integral method, impact energy fracture toughness correlations
Fatigue corrosion cracking, stress corrosion cracking
bibliography: Richard W. Hertzberg, Richard P. Vinci, Jason L. Hertzberg, Deformation and Fracture Mechanics of Engineering Materials, Wiley, USA
E.E. Gdoutos, Fracture Mechanics, Kluwer Academic Publishing, Boston, 1993.
